text: Which project is commercialising a drive-by-wire system for the steer, brake and gas functions of a production car so that people with a wide range of physical disabilities can drive using joysticks or handlebars instead of conventional controls, with the same modular system also serving teleoperated and autonomous off-highway vehicles?
reference_answer: Joysteer 3.0. The project is bringing to market a modular drive-by-wire system covering the steer, brake and gas functions of a vehicle: electronic driving systems plus individually adapted man-machine interfaces such as joysticks or handlebars take the place of the conventional controls, so that people with a wide range of disabilities can drive an adapted standard production car with fast, redundant and predictable response. The same modular architecture, extended with remote GPS-based access, is aimed at teleoperated and autonomous vehicles that remove workers from risky off-highway settings such as construction, mining, agriculture-forestry, airport handling and rescue.
notes: Seed: 807968, the only project tagged euroSciVoc leaf 'drive by wire' (re-executed this pass: COUNT(DISTINCT projectID)=1). text: How do EU-funded projects that set out to measure a property of the antihydrogen atom itself differ in which property each aims to measure and by what apparatus?
reference_answer: Two projects set out to measure a property of antihydrogen itself, and they target different properties with different apparatus. ANGRAM aimed at a 30% measurement of the gravitational acceleration for antihydrogen - enough to reveal the sign of gravity acting on antimatter and test the Weak Equivalence Principle - by rotating a three-grating moire deflectometer coupled to a detector, a scheme that requires neither position resolution nor time-of-flight information; the atoms were to be made in the AEgIS apparatus by three-body recombination of antiprotons and positrons, but only a signal consistent with production of antihydrogen atoms was reported, after the end of the beam time, so the gravity measurement could not be carried out, and the project further found that Rydberg-state antihydrogen interacts too heavily with the atoms of material gratings for material gratings to be usable. QUARTET measures a spectroscopic property instead: the classical Lamb shift, a transition in the microwave region, with antihydrogen spectroscopy planned on the ELENA beamline at CERN alongside a parallel muonium campaign at PSI; if no difference from matter is observed the measurement gives the first determination of the antiproton charge radius. Their apparatus differs accordingly - a rotating grating interferometer and annihilation detector for the free-fall measurement in ANGRAM, a microwave spectroscopy setup commissioned with protons and then adapted to the GBAR beamline for QUARTET.
notes: Seeds from corpus-profile candidate vector-53 (antihydrogen), re-executed this pass: SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%antihydrogen%' -> 721559 AVA, 748826 ANGRAM, 101019414 QUARTET (3 rows, unchanged). All three read in full via get_project_text before the question existed. Gold is the two that measure a property of the anti-atom itself. Pooled search on the final question text, k=10, all four conditions, 22 distinct projects. IN: 748826 ANGRAM (objective: 30% measurement of the gravitational acceleration for antihydrogen with a rotating three-grating moire deflectometer); 101019414 QUARTET (objective: Antihydrogen spectroscopy on the ELENA beamline, classical Lamb-Shift in the microwave region, antiproton charge radius). OUT with reason: 721559 AVA - names CPT tests by high-resolution spectroscopy on antihydrogen as motivating physics but measures no antihydrogen property itself; its executed work is antiproton beam lifetime and cooling at ELENA and LEIR, beam diagnostics, a Penning-trap antiproton heating-rate measurement and Timepix3 antiproton tagging; 804383 ANTI-ATOM - positron/positronium many-body theory, antihydrogen named once in the report summary as background on what other laboratories study; 742247 XUV-COMB - He+ 1S-2S XUV frequency-comb spectroscopy, anti-hydrogen named only as the alternative not taken; 852818 STEP - Penning-trap CPT and cyclotron-frequency measurements on single antiprotons; 832848 FunI - Penning-trap magnetic moments and masses of (anti)protons and highly charged ions; 726276 PUMA - antiproton-nucleus annihilation to probe neutron halos; 695677 QED-PROTONSIZE and 725039 HyperMu - ordinary and muonic hydrogen spectroscopy, matter not antimatter; 804815 MEGANTE - rubidium atom interferometry for the gravitational constant; 679038 MIRACLS - collinear laser spectroscopy of radionuclides; 950692 CosmicAntiNuclei - antideuteron production in collisions; 716651 NEDM - neutron electric dipole moment; 670168 NEWPHYS-MOLECULES - H2/D2/HD frequency measurements; 947696 YbFUN - parity violation in ytterbium; 818053 Mu-MASS - muonium laser spectroscopy, no antihydrogen in objective or report; 805065 HydMet, 948240 UniRand, 658556 NanoBragg, 656485 SPIN3, 674960 ASPIRE, 843554 BIOMOSAIC, 101030985 RADICEL, 863490 GyroSCoPe, 101023589 CLAVHUB, 660083 MEMDYN, 724932 MECHANICS, 864792 OXYGEN - clearly off-topic from their best chunk. Completeness sweep (non-embedding, run_sql): (a) project.objective and report_text (teaser+summary+workPerformed+finalResults) ILIKE any of '%antihydrogen%','%anti-hydrogen%','%antiatom%','%anti-atom%' -> exactly 5 projects corpus-wide: 721559 AVA, 742247 XUV-COMB, 748826 ANGRAM, 804383 ANTI-ATOM, 101019414 QUARTET; only ANGRAM and QUARTET measure a property of the anti-atom. (b) project.objective ILIKE '%antiproton%' OR '%antimatter%' OR '%antiprotonic%' -> 42 projects; the antimatter-experiment members (PUMA 726276, STEP 852818, FunI 832848) were read and none measures a property of antihydrogen. term_style exact-term: 'antihydrogen' appears verbatim in both gold objectives; the rank matrix agrees - lexical ranks ANGRAM 1 and QUARTET 2 on the question text.

text: Which EU-funded projects put in place, as part of their own work, engineered planted treatment systems for wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - beds, ponds or modules filled with gravel, sand or soil and planted with vegetation, through which the water to be cleaned is passed so that the plants and the microbes around their roots do the treating with little or no energy input? I mean a unit the project itself builds, operates or tests during the grant, not natural marshes being studied or restored, and not planted drainage features installed to manage rainwater runoff for flood or heat resilience.
reference_answer: Fifteen EU-funded projects build, run or test such a unit. A decentralised, near-zero-energy sewage strand is the largest: iMETland built a full-scale device to treat urban wastewater from small communities at zero-energy operation cost by combining electroactive bacteria and an electroconductive material with the biofilter bed, reaching depuration rates 10-fold higher than classical techniques; ELECTRAMMOX extends that METland concept to anaerobic ammonium oxidation for N removal from sewage; ELECTRA ran electrochemically enhanced versions that improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw or secondary treated municipal wastewater; and alchemia-nova's VertECO work develops indoor and outdoor plant-based units for household grey-water. Others target a named contaminant or water source: ZIRONITRO's planted ponds remove nitrate from groundwater (98% removal, 84% lower cost than current solutions), TOXICROP reports toxic cyanobacteria clearance rates on the order of 94% and about 99% removal rates of the toxin microcystins, INDIA-H2O validated phyto-treatment in a small wetland construction and then a larger constructed system for saline groundwater and industrial wastewater in Gujarat, and M2EX used such beds to polish bioleaching effluent until it was suitable for irrigation. The rest embed them in larger treatment trains: AquaNES combines them with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, HYDROUSA couples them with anaerobic processes and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, INCOVER runs them as one of the resource-recovery technologies validated at demo scale in Spain and Germany, PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands+' in real Indian environments, MULTISOURCE monitored seven such pilots for wastewater parameters, microplastics and pathogens, NICE constructed 15 pilots across 10 urban sites covering wastewater, greywater and combined sewer overflow, and WATERAGRI tested farm-scale versions for water quality and nutrient recovery from agricultural catchments.
notes: Membership test, stated in the question text and applied in both directions in one pass: the project ITSELF builds, operates or tests a planted treatment unit (bed, pond or module of gravel/sand/soil with vegetation) during the grant, and the water passed through it is wastewater, sewage or otherwise polluted water - not natural marshes studied or restored, and not planted drainage features for rainwater runoff managed for flood or heat resilience. Seeds: the six projects whose objective/title carry the specialist label (642190, 689450, 701542, 773351, 858375, 894525); drift check re-executed and returned exactly those six. FIX ROUND CHANGES. (1) 854782 M-NBS removed from gold: its whole workPerformed is commercial ('During Phase 1 we have carried out a thorough market analysis to select our target countries ... a well-defined commercial strategy ... confirmed our Freedom to Operate and analyzed the relevant regulation concerning the transport of our modules ... rethought our supply chain'), and the deployments its objective claims predate the grant ('has been successfully applied NBS in more than 100 large scale natural sanitation and remediation projects as non-mobile unit'). No unit built or operated under the grant is stated, so it fails the physical test. (2) 101000348 DIVAGRI re-argued against the sentence the critic named rather than against its framing: it PASSES the own-work half of the test ('Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites ... include ... artificial wetland'; 'All seven bio-based technologies will be installed at all pilot sites within the next few months'), and is excluded only on the water half - the sole sentence assigning that unit a duty calls it a water SAVING technology ('Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers') and no polluted water stream is named anywhere in its text. (3) The water being treated is now in the question text, so 730283 GROW GREEN is decided on text a system sees: its constructed features are raingardens, swales, tree pits, permeable pavements and infiltration trenches created to 'adapt cityscapes to a climate change', in cities that 'already experience flooding and heat stress' - runoff managed for flood and heat resilience, excluded. Rain-garden / bioretention / swale / SuDS sweep (objective + all report sections, terms: rain garden, raingarden, swale, bioretention, bio-retention, sustainable urban drainage, SuDS) returned 11 projects, all adjudicated: 101003765 NICE IN (see below), 730283 GROW GREEN OUT (runoff for climate resilience), 786566 Mind4Stormwater OUT (asset MANAGEMENT of existing stormwater control measures - 'their long-term management is far from assured' - builds nothing and the water is stormwater), 641931 CENTAUR OUT (real-time control of sewer networks to reduce urban flood risk; no planted unit), 101008626 Co-UDlabs OUT (transnational access to urban-drainage research facilities), 867798 Bufferblock OUT (plastic/concrete drainage blocks under roads for buffering, no vegetation), and 633125 EUCYS 2014, 754475 HD-App, 947761 AGING MATTERS, 101028810 ATTENTIVE, 101031317 EstroGen, 101036560 REGILIENCE OUT as substring false matches with no water-treatment content. Stormwater-adjacent gold re-confirmed on treatment evidence, not runoff evidence: NICE on 'hybrid subsurface wetlands' plus pilots 'covering the urban water cycle (wastewater, greywater, river basins, stormwater & combined sewer overflow)' - its rain gardens are not what carries it; MULTISOURCE on 'seven NBS pilots ... monitored for global wastewater parameters, microplastics, and pathogens' and its treatment-wetlands work. 858375 WATERAGRI kept on 'farm constructed wetlands' tested under objective (d) with a stated water-quality and nutrient-recovery duty ('improving water quality and nutrient uptake by crops', 'enhanced nutrient recovery from streams'), i.e. polluted water, not flood-resilience drainage. Other OUT decisions (unchanged by the narrowing, all re-checked against the new water clause on quoted text held from this session): 701542 UMIC (natural-wetland uranium colloid geochemistry), 660391 OPTWET (wetland restoration siting), 642228 SUBSOL, 704957 NANOREM, 751692 BIRDBARRIER, 788009 IRMIDYN, 817155 Aqua Gratis (grey-water recycling by biocide dosing, no planted stage), 858378 EPSETECH, 734409 Water4Cities, 842460 PROTEAN, 101006717 CERESiS and 826312 GREENER (soil phytoremediation), 101028018 SPONGE, 101036484 WaterLANDS (natural wetland restoration), 689817 INNOQUA (earthworm lumbrifilter), 821423 SPRING (EU-India biotechnical water treatment; none of the four term sweeps - wetland variants, phyto/planted-filter, nature-based-solution family, CW abbreviation - match its text, so no planted unit is evidenced), and the reactor/membrane/algal/sludge water-treatment projects and unrelated noise in the k=25 pool (InnoPellet, RECOPHARMA, POWERSTEP, SMART-Plant, AMBI-ROBIC, CLEAR, CPB 4.0, ACT, RichWater, EKO_MEMOF, ECWRTI, EBBR, SHEPHERD, KATEDRAL, IDESoWa, WISEFLOW, algaPLUS, PROMISCES, FireAndRiskPrevention, Project O, CleanHydro, SOLWARIS, RECYCLES, BALANCE, MIDES, HARM, PHARM AD, BioMAX, HTSew, Res2Pel, Ko-Tsah-To).
